judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard notice mechanics; "deemed properly given when delivered" covers each listed method plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Company address block names only Ajuba International, not Ajuba India, though Ajuba India is half of the defined "Company" and the payer under §2.2 — a minor gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain withholding clause tied to "as required by law".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Payments are made by Ajuba India to an India-resident employee while the clause speaks of "federal, state and local" taxes, a mismatch with the preamble and §8.2's "state or federal laws" references.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the ongoing provisions of this Agreement" is circular and identifies no provisions — a genuinely vague survival clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Which covenants survive matters directly for Articles III, IV and V and for §1.14's post-term Restricted Period, and no other clause supplies the list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The merger language is standard, but the carve-out "except for that certain Non-Competition Agreement of even date herewith" is an unspecified external document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That preserved agreement sits alongside Article V's own restraints and §6.1's representation that Employee is subject to no non-compete, raising a real question which covenant governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the Parties" is capitalised but never defined in this Agreement (only in Exhibit A), a small definitional slip in an otherwise clear clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Making Parent a beneficiary fits §1.5, §1.7 and Article V(b), which impose duties running to Parent; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear Michigan choice of law excluding renvoi.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Employment is by an Indian company of an India-resident, and §9.6/§8.2 reference federal and state law, but nothing in the instrument contradicts the choice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate with a single meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The signature pages are duplicated and incomplete, but that is an execution fact, not a clause conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of transfer types preceded by "Except as may be contrary to applicable law"; plain enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with §9.4's ban on assignment by the Employee; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "disparage" is undefined and open-ended, the obligation is perpetual ("and thereafter"), and the sentence has no terminal punctuation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A ¶3 states a differently scoped non-disparagement duty limited to "so long as Employee holds Restricted Stock Units" and asymmetric as between the parties, which pulls against this mutual perpetual version.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow recusal undertaking with a clear trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with §8.4(b), which contemplates his Board membership and its removal.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "may be brought against any of parties in the courts of" is both permissive (may) and grammatically defective, so whether this is an exclusive forum clause or a mere consent to jurisdiction is squarely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the only forum provision and must be read with §9.10 (Michigan law) and Exhibit A ¶17; the consent-to-jurisdiction reading is what a jurisdictional motion in this very case would turn on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals contain unfilled blanks, a mislabelled recital ("OF" for C) and garbled text ("employment at band separation from Comnipany").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recital D describes a settlement of "any and all claims" while operative ¶1 expressly excludes claims to compel amounts due under the Employment Agreement — a recital/operative divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very long "any and all ... including, but not limited to" catalogue of statutes closed by "excluding only those to compel the payment of amounts due" — the interaction of the catch-all and the single carve-out is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out has to be squared with §8.4, which makes severance conditional on this release, and with Exhibit A ¶19's forfeiture on violation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated list ends in "all other assets, materials and information of any kind or nature, belonging or pertaining to Company", an unbounded catch-all defining the returnable property.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps but does not match §3.2 (Confidential Information) and §4.2 (Company Technology), so three differently defined return obligations coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is conditioned on "so long as Employee holds Restricted Stock Units" — a concept found nowhere in this instrument — and assumes a "resignation" though the release may follow a Company termination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts §9.13's mutual, perpetual non-disparagement covenant in both duration and scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To never seek or accept employment with Company." is a subjectless fragment with no promisor named, a mechanical defect that obscures who is bound and on what terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A perpetual bar on re-employment sits oddly with Exhibit A ¶6, which obliges the Employee to give continuing assistance and consultative advice to the Company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short acknowledgment that tracks Articles III, IV and V by subject matter rather than by citation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves obligations that Exhibit A ¶15's entire-agreement clause might otherwise be read to supersede, so the two need harmonising.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "reasonable notice" and "more than a reasonable amount of the Employee's time" are soft but ordinary standards, and reimbursement is expressly promised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the Employment Agreement or the rest of the Release contradicts a post-termination cooperation duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain factual acknowledgment cross-referring to paragraph 1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with ¶1's release; no competing provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard ADEA-style acknowledgment, unambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with ¶¶9, 10 and 12 of the Release.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed 21-day consideration period; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 21-day and 7-day periods together delay severance under §8.4 of the Employment Agreement, but the timing is compatible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The addressee and hand-delivery blanks are unfilled, so the mechanics for an effective revocation cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with ¶11's written-confirmation condition, but the blanks make it uncertain how the condition can be satisfied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the Company's obligations" is unqualified — arguably all obligations, not only severance, despite the heading limiting it to severance payments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §8.4 conditions severance only on "execution without revocation" of the release, saying nothing about the further written-confirmation requirement added here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Routine voluntariness acknowledgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with ¶¶8, 9 and 15 of the Release.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Company's carve-out for "legitimate business purposes" is an undefined, self-judging exception against the Employee's near-absolute duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors §3.3 of the Employment Agreement but sits against ¶3, which separately limits what the Company may say about the Employee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-sentence non-admission clause with a settled meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision cuts against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "regarding the matters set forth herein" leaves the scope of the integration uncertain, and a comma splice joins the two sentences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with ¶5 (continuing Employment Agreement obligations) and with §9.8 of the Employment Agreement, which itself carves out a separate Non-Competition Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional newly-discovered-facts clause supporting the release.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with ¶1's "known or unknown" release language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and unambiguous Michigan choice-of-law clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches §9.10 of the Employment Agreement; the Release simply has no forum clause of its own.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard reformation-or-excision severability language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Slightly different from §9.2 of the Employment Agreement (excision only) and Article VII (judicial modification of restraints), but the three operate on different documents/provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It releases the Company from obligations "under the Severance Agreement", a document this instrument never defines (it is the "Release"), and the sentence ends in a comma without completion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The forfeiture also collides with ¶1's carve-out preserving claims "to compel the payment of amounts due to Employee as provided in the Employment Agreement" and with §8.4's severance promise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Responsible for providing recommendations" with an "including" list is broad but describes an advisory role clearly enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §2.1 says he reports to the Board while this line has him advise the Chairman and the Board; §8.4(a) then treats removal of certain functions as non-diminution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense run-on list whose parenthetical "(including Ajuba US and all subsidiaries)" leaves unclear how far his finance/cash-management authority reaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §8.4(a) expressly says consolidation, elimination or outsourcing of cash management, accounting and sales and marketing is not a material diminution, and §2.1 deems Schedule 2.1 amended accordingly — so the duties granted here can be stripped without breach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "directly or indirectly" reporting is a plain organisational statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It can be undone by the §2.1/§8.4(a) deemed-amendment mechanism and by §8.4's final sentence allowing his title to be reduced to Senior Vice President after year one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-word reporting line, definite as far as it goes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §2.1 says "Employee shall report directly to the Board (or selected designee of the Board of Directors of the Parent)", which is a different reporting relationship from the Chairman named here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple quarterly attendance duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with §9.14's recusal provision and §8.4(b)'s reference to Board membership.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It mixes an obligation ("Employee shall oversee") with non-binding estimates, but the completion test — last to occur of four dated events — is objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §2.2(f) pays the $200,000 "when and if" the UK office "is shut down" per this Schedule, yet the completion events (employee departures, lease termination) are within Ajuba's control, not Employee's.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Restructure" is defined only as termination of a named lease, which is narrower than the ordinary meaning of restructuring the office.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §2.2(f) conditions the Reorganization Bonus on the Novi office being "restructured" in accordance with this Schedule, so the mismatch in meaning bears directly on the payment trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disclaims any representation while referring to "Contemplated Transactions (as defined in the Stock Purchase Agreement dated June __, 2005)" — an undefined external term with a blank date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §2.2(f) describes this Schedule as one "which sets forth the specific cost savings for each action and a reasonable risk assessment", which pulls against a clause saying the figures are mere good-faith estimates with no warranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, absolute cost-allocation sentence with little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It places costs on "Ajuba" alone although the preamble defines "Company" as Ajuba and Ajuba India and §2.2(f) has Ajuba India pay the Reorganization Bonus.
